transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (SE), Priya Nair (SE); Rajiv Patel (NimbusAir Head of Data), Leah Morgan (ML Eng), Carlos Mendes (PM), Sofia Ruiz (Security)

Summary (auto):
- POC scoping for an NLP assistant across support/reservations and ops transcripts (multilingual: EN/ES/PT).
- Objective to shortlist 2-3 open models for a 2-week POC with clear benchmarks (latency, quality, cost).
- Benchmarks to run on Redwood hosted and Dedicated variants; customer to provide prompts and sample logs.

Topics covered: success criteria, throughput and sizing, model shortlist options, multilingual and domain adaption, compliance/VPC questions, timeline and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick intros?
[00:08] Rajiv: Hi all, Rajiv here, head of data at NimbusAir. We're trying to prototype an assistant for agents and ops that can read reservation notes and surface policy guidance.
[00:20] Leah: Leah, ML engineer on the team, I'll own the evaluation and data prep.
[00:25] Carlos: Carlos, product, focused on success criteria and timelines.
[00:29] Sofia: Sofia, security architect, I'm here for compliance questions.
[00:33] Diego: Diego from Redwood SE team. I will run the benchmark configs and help with model selection.
[00:38] Priya: Priya, inference SE, will cover latency/cost tradeoffs and deployment options.

[00:45] Maya: Cool. High level — the customer's ask is a POC to validate three things: 1) model quality on domain-specific reservation notes in EN/ES/PT, 2) latency under peak contact center load, and 3) per-token cost and ops for a pilot. We want to land on 2-3 open models for the pilot.

[01:02] Carlos: Quick question on traffic shape — we're expecting episodes around 120 QPS at peak? but mostly bursty during check-in windows. Rajiv, is that right?
[01:12] Rajiv: Yeah, ballpark. Peak concurrency ~80-120 concurrent agent sessions; average session is small — maybe 70 tokens per turn, but multi-turn dialogs. Monthly token estimate roughly 200M tokens for the pilot footprint.
[01:29] Priya: That's helpful. For a 2-week POC we'll scale down to a representative 48-hour run that simulates those bursts. We'll need the prompt distribution and a synthetic traffic file.
[01:39] Leah: We'll provide 500-1,000 prompts across intents and the top 50 reservation note templates. We'll redact PHI and share the schema.

[01:46] Diego: For model shortlist, we're proposing open models with strong multilingual coverage and good instruction-following. Initial candidates: Llama2-based 70B quantized variant, Mistral-instruct 7B/Chat variants, and Redmond-open-34B (placeholder name) — note: names in the transcript may be garbled from the call. We also talked about a smaller 13B variant to compare latency.
[02:10] Carlos: Can you speak to quality tradeoffs? We care more about correctness than flair — hallucinations are a showstopper.
[02:17] Diego: Right. So tradeoffs: larger models (34B+) have better factuality on long reservation contexts but cost more; 13B models are cheaper and faster but need prompt engineering and retrieval augmentation to hit the same correctness. We can also test retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to reduce hallucinations.
[02:37] Rajiv: Are we considering fine-tuning vs prompt tuning? We want to avoid long retrain cycles.
[02:42] Priya: For POC it's cleaner to use prompt + RAG, maybe LoRA on a single checkpoint if we need more domain adaptation. Full fine-tune increases ops and latency complexity for the POC.

[02:55] Sofia: Security — will data leave our VPC? What are options for private deployments?
[02:59] Maya: We offer Hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool with tenant isolation), and Private/VPC (customer-managed networking). For POC we usually run hosted or dedicated in a customer-dedicated tenant. We can also run a private control plane if required.
[03:18] Sofia: Does Redwood support KMS integrations and HSM?
[03:21] Priya: Yes, we support KMS for keys and can integrate with customer HSMs for Private deployments. Audit logs and per-token tracing are available; we'll share the security pack.

[03:30] Carlos: Benchmarking specifics — what metrics will you collect?
[03:33] Diego: We'll measure p50/p90/p99 latency per token and per request, throughput (QPS), token/sec GPU, and cost per generated token. On quality we'll run accuracy and a domain-specific correctness rubric (binary correct/incorrect for policy answers), plus n-gram overlap is not sufficient, so we'll include human evals on a 200-sample set.
[03:54] Leah: For multilingual, how do you handle tokenization differences that affect latency and cost? Spanish and Portuguese can be slightly longer in tokens.
[04:01] Priya: We'll include language buckets in the benchmark and report cost and latency per language. Also watch out for sequence length distribution differences; we'll sample by language and adjust batch sizes accordingly.

[04:15] [04:15] (murmur) Speaker 1: right
[04:18] Diego: Example benchmark plan: 48-hour run, three model variants (34B quantized, 13B fast, 7B Mistral-instruct), two deployment modes (hosted shared, hosted-dedicated), concurrency profile mixing steady 20 QPS with bursts to 120 QPS, and human eval slices for correctness.
[04:38] Rajiv: Do you have priors on latency? Our SLA target is <400ms p90 end-to-end for single-turn lookups.
[04:47] Priya: For the 13B with aggressive quantization you might see p90 ~350-450ms depending on sequence length; 34B models often hit 500-700ms unless pinned on dedicated GPUs with optimized kernels. We'll test both and report cost per response.
[05:05] Carlos: What's the cost delta? very rough numbers are fine.
[05:08] Maya: Short answer: 13B quant/7B will be substantially cheaper — think 3-6x lower per token vs 34B class. We'll produce a comparison table in the benchmark results.
[05:18] Leah: On hallucinations, will you run a regression suite with our critical prompts?
[05:22] Diego: Yes, include your critical prompts in the human eval set. We can also run automated checks for contradictory responses and fuzzy match to ground-truth.

[05:30] Rajiv: For the POC success criteria, we propose: 1) p90 latency < 500ms for EN; 2) domain-correctness >= 92% on the human eval set; 3) cost per 1k tokens below our threshold (we'll confirm in doc). If we meet those, we move to pilot.
[05:48] Carlos: Timeline — how long until we have results?
[05:50] Maya: Once prompts and synthetic traffic are in (target 9/8), Redwood will configure the benchmark the week of 9/8, run 48-hour runs by 9/10-9/12, and deliver results and a walkthrough by 9/15. Pilot kickoff tentatively late September.
[06:06] Sofia: On compliance, we need evidence of SOC2 plus the network architecture for Dedicated and Private. Also SAML SSO for console access.
[06:16] Priya: We'll attach SOC2 report and a VPC deployment diagram. SSO/SAML is supported; we can map roles for console and API keys.

[06:25] [06:25] (crosstalk) Speaker 2: yeah, that's fine
[06:29] Diego: A few technical notes on the benchmark: we'll test sequence lengths 32/128/512 and measure KV cache behavior for multi-turn. For reservation notes we expect longer contexts up to 1K tokens occasionally; we'll include tail-case runs.
[06:48] Leah: We'll also need to test retrieval augmentation latency — adding a 3-5 doc retrieval step could add 40-120ms; we need to budget for that.
[06:58] Priya: Correct. For RAG we measure end-to-end latencies with retrieval, re-ranking (if used), and generation. Redwood supports function/tool calling so you can plug in your retriever; we'll show examples.

[07:10] Carlos: Any blockers for running the POC on Redwood hosted?
[07:13] Maya: Only access and data — we need the prompt set, synthetic traffic, and an API key. If you need VPC-only, that will add lead time for networking and security reviews.
[07:25] Sofia: For data residency, can you limit logs and store audit logs in our account?
[07:28] Priya: Yes for Dedicated/Private we can forward or store logs into your S3 and integrate with KMS; hosted shared will have retention policies but we can set shortened retention for POC. We'll include retention options in the security pack.

[07:40] Rajiv: A pragmatic question — which model would you start with for the first run if we only had to pick one?
[07:46] Diego: I'd start with the 13B quantized Mistral-instruct variant to validate latency and cost, paired with RAG. If accuracy is borderline then swap to the 34B for the 48-hour run. That gets you a fast signal.
[07:57] Leah: Makes sense — we can validate correctness quickly and then decide.

[08:02] Maya: We'll also produce a recommended prompt engineering checklist and a warmup script to prefill KV cache before the burst windows. That helps with p90.
[08:12] Carlos: On evaluation, curious about automated metrics vs human evaluation weight — what's typical?
[08:16] Diego: For domain tasks we usually weight human eval 70% and automated checks 30% for final success criteria, because automated metrics often miss domain correctness. We can adjust per your preference.

[08:28] [08:28] (brief pause)
[08:32] Sofia: Regarding access control, can API keys be scoped per environment and revoked centrally?
[08:36] Priya: Yes, API keys can be scoped and rotated. We also support RBAC in the console and can disable keys programmatically.

[08:44] Rajiv: If we do a Private deployment after the POC, what kind of timeline are we looking at?
[08:50] Maya: Private deployments can be 6-10 weeks depending on network approvals and on-prem provisioning; Dedicated you can get in a few weeks if capacity is available. We'll include a deployment timeline in the POC packet.

[09:02] Carlos: Any thoughts on caching strategies? Reservation notes often repeat phrases — prefix caching could help.
[09:08] Diego: Yes, prefix/KV caching is one of our levers. We'll also suggest intelligent batching windows to reduce per-token overhead without blowing latency SLOs. We'll show cost delta in the benchmark report.

[09:20] Leah: For the human eval, we'll need a labeling rubric. Can Redwood provide a template?
[09:24] Maya: Yes, we'll share a rubric and a recommended 200-sample labeling plan. We can also run the first batch of human evals if you want us to.

[09:34] Diego: Quick note — some model names may be off in the transcript; in the benchmark config we'll list exact checkpoints and quantization knobs.

[09:40] [09:40] (laughter)
[09:42] Carlos: Alright, let's recap and lock next steps.
[09:45] Maya: Recap: Redwood runs a 48-hour benchmark with 3 model variants, two deployment modes, and language buckets. Customer provides prompts and synthetic traffic by 9/8. Redwood sends security pack and sample benchmark config by 9/4. Results walkthrough by 9/15.
[09:59] Rajiv: Agreed. Also Rajiv asks Redwood to include cost per 1k tokens and an estimate for scaling to full pilot.
[10:07] Maya: Noted. Any other questions?
[10:10] Sofia: Please include SAML and KMS integration steps in the packet.
[10:14] Maya: Will do.
[10:16] Carlos: That's all from product. Thanks everyone.
[10:19] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with the benchmark plan and a calendar invite for the walkthrough.
[10:25] (meeting ends)
